approachQuestion.prompt:
Repairing a Display

A display string contains only ( and ). Delete the fewest characters needed to leave a string whose every prefix has nonnegative balance and whose final balance is zero. Return every distinct resulting string, once; an empty result string is allowed.

Examples:
s="())" -> ["()"].
s=")(" -> [""].
s="()())()" -> ["(())()","()()()"].

Constraints: 0 <= n=s.length <= 20. Relative order of retained characters cannot change.

options.text: Compute unmatched opening/closing deletion counts first. Explore keeping or deleting each character while spending exactly those counts and maintaining nonnegative kept-prefix balance. Deduplicate completed strings with a character trie.
options.feedback: The unmatched counts are necessary and sufficient minimum deletions for one bracket type. Exact budgets ensure optimality; the trie merges equal strings arising from deleting interchangeable positions.

options.text: At every negative prefix delete the first closing symbol encountered, then delete all remaining unmatched openings, returning only that one repair.
options.feedback: This can find one minimum repair but does not enumerate all distinct answers, as shown by the two answers for "()())()".

options.text: Accept any balanced subsequence, regardless of how many deletions it used.
options.feedback: For s="()", returning "" violates the minimum-deletion requirement; no deletion is needed.

options.text: Enumerate every retained-index subset, validate its string, keep those with the fewest deletions, and deduplicate completed strings in a trie.
options.feedback: This is correct but explores nonminimum deletion counts and negative prefixes that exact budgets and balance checks can eliminate.

feedback.reason: The unmatched counts are necessary and sufficient minimum deletions for one bracket type. Exact budgets ensure optimality; the trie merges equal strings arising from deleting interchangeable positions.
details: Scan once to count unmatched closing and opening symbols: these are required close/open deletion budgets. Recursively process each character, either delete it if its matching budget remains or keep it if balance stays nonnegative. At the end accept only zero budgets and zero balance. Insert a copied result into a character trie to remove duplicate strings.

Minimal unmatched-open/close counts fix deletion budgets before search. Preserve nonnegative kept balance and require zero final balance. Different deletion choices can yield the same repaired string, so the trie deduplicates actual outputs.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-12-search` only. Let V count recursive calls and K count characters copied and examined during all accepted-leaf insertions into the deduplication trie, including duplicate insertions. Trie children are two fixed slots and terminal flags; let U be the number of trie nodes allocated, including the root. The trie is auxiliary deduplication storage. Append a copied string to the returned list only on its first insertion. Scan s once before recursion. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n + V + K) time, O(n + U) auxiliary space
O(n + V) time, O(n + U) auxiliary space
O(n + V + K) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n² + K) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Include the initial scan, visited search states, and accepted-leaf trie character work.
details: Budget initialization scans n characters. Each search call makes at most two constant-cost transitions, and accepted leaves perform K total trie/copy character operations. Empty-string insertions cost constant per leaf, already bounded by V.
The active buffer and stack need linear space in n. The auxiliary trie retains U fixed-size nodes across branches; the returned string list is separate and excluded.

Let V count recursive calls and K count characters copied and examined during all accepted-leaf insertions into the deduplication trie, including duplicate insertions. Trie children are two fixed slots and terminal flags; let U be the number of trie nodes allocated, including the root. The trie is auxiliary deduplication storage. Append a copied string to the returned list only on its first insertion. Scan s once before recursion.
“O(n + V) time, O(n + U) auxiliary space”: Repeated accepted strings still require trie traversal, counted by K.
“O(n + V + K) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The deduplication trie is auxiliary storage and can contain U nodes across branches.
“O(n² + K) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The exact-budget search can branch over many deletion position choices.
